sections.title: ML: Tech Law, IP and Emerging AI Intensive (McNichol)
sections.description:
Intellectual Property law has long been a means to advance social policy. IP law is used to encourage unexpected innovations, to encourage some kinds of economic activity, and to discourage others. IP law accomplishes this by giving exclusive rights to persons who make socially valuable contributions. These exclusive rights are patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, the right of publicity, and a few other less well-known forms of commercial exclusivity. This course explores these exclusive rights, how they are acquired, and how IP law balances the social and economic burdens imposed by even temporary monopolies against the benefits of advancing social goals and policies.
This course follows an intensive format. The first class meeting will be a one-hour remote session that provides an overview of the course. The next class meetings will be two full weekend sessions, each meeting Saturday and Sunday from 8:30 to 5:00. Morning coffee and light lunches will be provided.
